Q1.statuteText: The goods must in terms of type, quantity, quality, other properties, and packaging conform to what follows from the contract.
Q1.question: Subjective Requirement Check
Q1.description: Does the good fail to match the quantity, quality, packaging, or description explicitly agreed upon in the contract or sales receipt?
Q1.onTrueGround: Defective under Chapter 4, Section 1 — Goods fail to conform with agreed contractual terms.

Q2.statuteText: The goods must be fit for the purposes for which corresponding goods are normally used, and possess the durability and functionality the buyer can reasonably expect.
Q2.question: Objective Requirement Check
Q2.description: Does the product fail normal expectations for fitness for standard purpose, durability, safety, or sample/model comparison?
Q2.onTrueGround: Defective under Chapter 4, Section 2 — Goods deviate from objective durability or standard fitness expectations.

Q3.statuteText: Goods are defective if they fail to conform to claims made in advertising, on packaging, or in public statements by the seller or manufacturer.
Q3.question: Marketing & Public Statements
Q3.description: Does the product fail to conform to specific claims made in marketing, on packaging, or in public statements by the seller or manufacturer?
Q3.onTrueGround: Defective under Chapter 4, Section 5 — Goods fail to match claims made in marketing or packaging.

Q4.statuteText: The seller is not liable for a deviation if the buyer was explicitly informed of the specific deviation and accepted it prior to purchase.
Q4.question: Explicit Pre-Sale Fault Disclaimer
Q4.description: Was the consumer explicitly informed of this specific fault prior to purchase and did they explicitly accept it?
Q4.onTrueGround: Exempted under Chapter 4, Section 6 — Consumer explicitly approved the specific deviation prior to sale.

Q5.statuteText: A defect exists if the goods were installed incorrectly by the seller, or if incorrect assembly instructions accompanied the goods.
Q5.question: Assembly & Installation Check
Q5.description: Was the defect caused by incorrect installation performed by the seller, or by faulty assembly instructions in the manual?
Q5.onTrueGround: Defective under Chapter 4, Section 3 — Defect resulted from faulty installation or incorrect assembly manual.

Q6.statuteText: The seller is liable for defects existing at delivery. Defects showing within two years (24 months) are presumed to have existed at delivery.
Q6.question: Timeframe & Presumption Period
Q6.description: Did the defect manifest within 2 years (24 months) from the date the product was delivered?
Q6.onTrueGround: Presumption Rule Active (Chapter 4, Section 17) — Defect manifested within 2 years and is presumed present at delivery.
Q6.onFalseGround: Presumption Window Expired (Chapter 4, Section 14) — Defect manifested after 2 years; burden of proof rests on consumer.

OUT_Defective.question: Defect Established
OUT_Defective.description: The product is deemed legally defective under Chapter 4 of the Consumer Sales Act.

OUT_NotDefective.question: No Statutory Defect Found
OUT_NotDefective.description: No statutory defects were identified under Chapter 4 of the Consumer Sales Act.
